comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the Forget slot fix is sound. `rightAction` is now a fixed `Style.space(22)` square, the glyph uses `anchors.centerIn: parent`, and the hover surface fills the same square, so glyph and hover box share one center. The panel side of Cancel is also wired as described: the connecting row stays clickable, the slot and the prompt show Cancel, the connect lane clears without recording a failure, other rows stay gated on `busy`, and Forget on other saved rows works on its own lane with its own 15 s timeout.

The Cancel action itself does not stop the connection attempt with the current Quickshell backend, and it introduces one destructive follow-on interaction. Details below.

### Cancel does not reach NetworkManager while a network is connecting

`cancelNetworkAction()` calls `network.disconnect()` ([Panel.qml L928-L936](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/989451c44d2f3ffd8fe3d0727d60f1d441678417/shell/plugins/panels/network/Panel.qml#L928-L936)). In Quickshell, [`Network::disconnect()`](https://github.com/quickshell-mirror/quickshell/blob/v0.3.1/src/network/network.cpp) returns early with "is not currently connected" unless `connected` is true, and the NetworkManager backend binds `connected` to the Activated state ([`src/network/nm/network.cpp`](https://github.com/quickshell-mirror/quickshell/blob/v0.3.1/src/network/nm/network.cpp), `NMNetwork::bindFrontend`). During "Connecting…" that guard stops the call, so `requestDisconnect` never fires and no D-Bus call is made. The same guard is present in v0.3.1 (the Arch package) and in current Quickshell master.

```text
Cancel (row click / slot / Enter / prompt button)
└─ cancelNetworkAction()
   ├─ network.disconnect()
   │   └─ Network::disconnect(): connected == false (still Activating)
   │       └─ return            ← no requestDisconnect, no Device.Disconnect
   └─ resetActionState() + refresh()   ← panel shows idle
NetworkManager: activation continues → a reachable network still connects
```

The `NMNetwork::requestDisconnect` → `NMDevice::disconnect` → `Device.Disconnect` chain cited in the PR discussion is accurate, but it only starts after this guard. A mock that accepts `disconnect()` on a network that is not yet connected cannot detect the gap.

**Impact:** Cancel resets the panel, but NetworkManager keeps activating. A user who picked the wrong network and pressed Cancel is still connected a few seconds later. With a wrong passphrase, NetworkManager keeps trying until its own timeout, and the panel silently drops that failure. The enterprise path behaves the same way on the NetworkManager side.

**Suggested change:** call a disconnect that is accepted while connecting, such as `network.device.disconnect()`. Quickshell's `NetworkDevice.disconnect()` only refuses the Disconnected and Disconnecting device states, and NetworkManager 1.58 honors `Device.Disconnect` for a pending activation. Two side effects are worth handling deliberately:
- A device-level disconnect blocks device autoconnect until the user activates a connection again.
- A Cancel pressed before NetworkManager has processed the activation request could act on the previously active connection. Gating Cancel on the device actually reporting a connecting state avoids that.

`nmcli connection down` on the specific profile is an alternative.

### After Cancel, the same slot becomes an armed Forget

Hovering the right-edge slot sets `wifiActionFocused = true`. `cancelNetworkAction()` does not clear it, and `onWifiNetworksChanged` keeps it because a saved, disconnected row is still forgettable. The re-created slot therefore shows an enabled, focused Forget in the position where Cancel just was.

| Slot state | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Saved row while connecting | disabled (`canForget && !root.busy`) | Cancel |
| Same slot right after Cancel | n/a | Forget, focused and enabled |
| Second click (MouseArea has no `onDoubleClicked`, so it emits `clicked` again) or second Enter | n/a | `forget()` runs |

**Impact:** a double-click on Cancel, or pressing Enter twice on the focused slot, deletes the saved profile without confirmation, and its passphrase or 802.1X credentials must be re-entered. Whether a particular physical double-click lands on the same row can depend on the list refresh, but a second delivered activation on the slot forgets the network.

**Suggested change:** clear `wifiActionFocused` in `cancelNetworkAction()`, or otherwise keep the slot from arming Forget immediately after a Cancel.

### Esc cannot abort a connect from the passphrase prompt

The new `Keys.onEscapePressed` branches on `idField` and `pwField` call `cancelNetworkAction()` when `row.isCancellable`. But `isCancellable` implies `row.isBusy`, and both fields are `enabled: !row.isBusy` (and hidden while busy). Qt Quick clears active focus when an item is disabled, so the fields cannot receive Esc in that state. `keyCatcher` is blocked while the prompt is open, and the prompt's Cancel button (`PanelActionButton`, `focusable: false` by default) cannot take keyboard focus.

**Impact:** there is no keyboard abort while the prompt is open. That covers new-network and wrong-passphrase connects, the main cases for cancelling. This is not a regression from base, but the Esc behavior described in the PR discussion does not occur.

**Suggested change:** provide a keyboard path that stays reachable while connecting. Possible approaches (untested): handle Esc on an item that stays enabled while the fields are disabled, or make the prompt's Cancel button keyboard-focusable.

### Cancelling an enterprise connect skips the helper's own cleanup

`enterpriseConnect.running = false` goes through Quickshell `Process::setRunning(false)` → `QProcess::terminate()`, which sends SIGTERM to the `bash -c` process only. The running `nmcli` step continues, and the script's `|| { nmcli connection delete uuid "$u"; false; }` branch in `Model.enterpriseConnectScript` never runs. A sandboxed probe with the same `a && b && long || { cleanup; false; }` shape, with a stand-in command in place of `nmcli`, showed exactly that: bash exited on SIGTERM, the child kept running, and the cleanup branch did not execute.

**Impact:** depending on timing, a cancelled 802.1X attempt can leave a profile without its password, or a failed profile that base would have deleted. The row can afterwards look saved with unusable credentials.

**Suggested change:** make cancellation run the same cleanup as a failure. Possible approaches (untested): a `TERM` trap in the helper script that deletes the partial profile, or stopping the helper's child processes as well as the shell.

**Keyboard connect during a pending Forget:** the new forget lane no longer sets `busy`, and `activateSelected()` does not check `forgetActive` or `forgetSsid`, unlike the row click, `submitCredentials` and the prompt Connect button. Enter on a row whose Forget is still pending starts a connect on the profile being deleted. The row then shows "Connecting…" until NetworkManager rejects or tears down the activation, or the 30 s timeout fires. On a default install the delete completes quickly, so this window is short. Returning early in `activateSelected()` when `forgetActive && forgetSsid === net.ssid` matches the mouse-path gating.

**`cancelledSsid` note:** the marker is only read to clear itself. Late outcomes after Cancel are silent because `resetActionState()` already cleared `actionKind` and `actionSsid`, not because of the marker. It is also reset when a new action starts, so it gives no protection when a same-SSID retry receives a late failure from the superseded attempt (a source-level possibility, not reproduced).

**Test coverage note:** all new `network-test.sh` assertions match `Panel.qml` source text. By reading, they pass with every issue above present. A few pin current behavior that a fix would change (the Esc handler text, the `cancelledSsid` assignments, the `enterpriseConnect.running = false` line).
